title: Compact requantization staging and prefill coordinator for mixed-precision streaming decode
creator: Asha Banerjee
description:
Problem: Dequantization/requantization overhead during streaming prefill and decode is a dominant CPU/GPU cost for mixed-precision (INT8/FP8) execution on customer workloads with many short requests and long context windows. Current runtime frequently performs full-batch dequant and per-layer casts even when only a small fraction of heads or tokens require higher precision, increasing latency tail and token cost.

Proposal: Implement a compact requantization staging layer (the 'staging coordinator') that sits between the KV cache prefill and kernel dispatcher. Key ideas: (1) Repack-window buffering — aggregate per-head precision needs across a short token window (configurable, default 4 tokens) and only materialize dequant/requant for heads that exceed a dynamic precision threshold. (2) Head-shard gating — track head-level error budgets and only promote heads to higher-precision kernels when the amortized approximation error exceeds the per-request budget. (3) Lazy micro-requant kernels — small, specialized microkernels that operate on packed head slices and support in-place requant with minimal memory traffic, invoked only for promoted slices. (4) Prefill-aware scheduling — prefill coordinator annotates each pending decode with a precision fingerprint; the kernel selector uses the fingerprint to pick a mixed-precision plan that minimizes dequant operations while meeting latency SLOs.

Why this is different: instead of treating dequantization as a coarse-grained one-shot operation, the staging coordinator treats precision transitions as local, temporal events and defers work until required. The solution emphasizes head-wise and token-window locality, small fast kernels to avoid full tensor broadcasts, and a tunable error budget so teams can trade cost for fidelity per-route.

Implementation scope: runtime layer changes (kernel selector, prefill coordinator), new microkernel library (CUDA/cuBLAS friendly patterns, fallback CPU stubs), telemetry hooks, and a canary rollout policy in console for per-route budget tuning. Backward compatibility: default to existing full-dequant path unless the route opts in (runtime config).

Risks and mitigations: risk of subtle numerical regressions on very sensitive tasks; mitigate by ship-with-eval-set gating, per-route regression alerts, and automatic rollback. Performance regressions due to poor microkernel packing: include microbench harness and CI perf gates.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end canary demonstrating >=15% GPU memory traffic reduction on representative decode workloads without >1% quality regression on route eval set
Prefill coordinator annotation is emitted for all streaming requests and honored by kernel selector
Microkernel library exposes in-place requant and head-slice ops with unit and microbench coverage
Telemetry dashboards show head-promotion rates, per-route cost delta, and SLO hit-rate; canary rollout blocked on regression alerts
Design doc and internal API reviewed and approved; PR merged and feature flag controllable per-route
comments: 2026-02-22: Spike complete — prototyped head-shard gating in python on top of perf traces. Observed 18-24% reduction in dequant bandwidth on short-request heavy traces when threshold tuned.
2026-03-01: Design review with Applied ML and Console teams. Feedback: need explicit per-route error budget and a clear UI for operators to tune the window size and promotion threshold.
2026-03-04: Engineering sync — agreed to implement microkernel as separate compile unit to allow hotfixing without full runtime rebuild. Liam to own CUDA impl; Angela to own CPU fallback.

2026-03-07: Benchmarks on p4d.24xlarge: naive full dequant baseline 1.0x decode bandwidth; staging-proto + microkernel 0.78x memory traffic and 0.91x end-to-end latency on median but 0.83x on 95th for short requests. Need to optimize microkernel launch overhead.
2026-03-10: PR #4862 opened for kernel-selector changes (WIP). Requests: add integration test for a 2-token prefetched window and mock head promotion to ensure no deadlocks in prefetch path.
2026-03-12: Product asked for toggle default-off and an admin console toggle for early enterprise customers. Added release gating and canary plan to acceptance criteria.
telemetry_checks: dequant_bandwidth_bytes(agg) — expect -15% improvement for canary cohort
decode_p95_latency — must not regress more than 10% for canary cohort
route_quality_regression — automatic alert if eval-set BLEU/ROUGE drops >1% or embedding drift >0.5 stddev
